In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of different amounts and periods of skim-milk feeding are not simple and are not easily interpreted.
skim-milk is a valuable addition to the diet of pigs up to about 75 lb. livewt. and that it can replace part or all of the meal allowance in the diet on a calculated drymatter basis.

the addition of liquid skim-millk to the diet of pigs up to 15¾ p.p.d. (pint per pig per day), and in particular up to a maximum level of 10¾ p.p.d., is beneficial in that it improves the carcass quality without adversely affecting the rate of growth or the carcass weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
skim-milk is an excellent supplement to a cereal-based diet and may be used at levels considerably in excess of those usually recommended without impairing performance or quality.
the quality of pork carcass is not adversely affected by giving liquid skim-milk in quantities up to 15¾ p.i. per pig per day and in fact may be improved.
the quality of the carcasses of pigs fed on a ration containing skim-milk was comparable with that of pigs fed on meal alone, and was in some respects better.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of liquid skim milk to the diet of pigs has a positive impact on carcass quality.
the addition of skim-milk to pig diets, up to a maximum level of 10 pints per pig daily, is not harmful to the carcass.
the quality of pork carcasses can be significantly improved by giving pigs liquid skim-milk in addition to their normal meal allowance.
